key_insight: Thermal and compositional buoyancy interact through a swallowtail onset geometry, producing kinked instability thresholds and selecting distinct Rossby waves rather than simply adding.
engineering_relevance: The results caution against additive-buoyancy approximations when predicting instability and competing flow patterns in rapidly rotating, double-diffusive fluids.
method: Analyze the rotating-annulus model’s exact cubic dispersion relation using the Bilharz stability criterion.
Derive rapid-rotation neutral-curve envelopes and their swallowtail geometry.
Evaluate nonlinear wave selection through mean-scalar feedback and cubic amplitude coefficients.
evidence_signal: Exact finite-rotation corner calculations and periodic-cell simulations confirm coexisting thermal and compositional waves and their invasion thresholds.
watch_item: The onset geometry is derived in a rapid-rotation annulus model; quantitative transfer to spherical shells or engineering systems requires validation.
paper_title: Thermochemical Rossby waves in rapid rotation: from swallowtail geometry to nonlinear selection
